stage1.impression: A Widmanstatten figure fills the frame under a green-edged clear layer on a pale cream ground, but the bands are one flat grey-green against flat charcoal, so the iron reads as a printed vector pattern, not etched metal. The only cues that it sits inside acrylic are one soft vertical streak and a mint rim on the right edge; two tan parallelograms float off the left edge for no reason.

blocking_9: Kamacite bands must read as metal: bands of different orientation differ by 40+ levels and the slice's interior lum_range exceeds 110 (now 89.7 in 1000,400-1300,700), with plessite fields darker than the bands by a factor of 3 or more.
The pocket's air rim must read silver all round, including the left edge, which is now a 5 px step straight from the sweep (237) to the rind (edge step -42.6), with no rim at all.
The frame must carry at least one unmistakable acrylic cue beyond the single streak: a curved highlight or the ball's contour so the viewer knows the iron is sealed in a ball.
No unexplained shapes: the two tan parallelograms at (205-250, 670-700) and (275-320, 800-820) must be gone.
The sweep behind must have tone and direction: the lower third is one value, 237 with range 2.8, and reads as blown paper.

changes.problem: The etch reads as a vector illustration: every kamacite band is the same grey-green with hard uniform edges and no orientation-dependent sheen, so it does not read as iron.

evidence.measured: lum_median 109, p5 56, p95 145, range 90; a single band (960,520-980,545) median 129, a plessite field (985,560-1010,600) median 61: two flat tones, ratio about 2:1; 3x crop shows bands with stamped dotted edges and no grain.

change.setting: slice etch surface (texture/material, shape and size unchanged)
change.to: a 4k scanned or photographed etched Gibeon slab mapped to the existing 62 x 44 mm face, with a per-band anisotropic roughness (0.15-0.35) whose direction follows each band's orientation, plessite fields roughness 0.5 and darker albedo, hairline taenite rims at roughness 0.1

changes.expected: Bands of the three orientations separate by 40+ levels under the same light; plessite stays near 45-60; fine grain visible at 3x.

changes.problem: The face of the slice sits low and grey: the brightest band tone is 145, far below the cream ground, so the iron has no shine to answer the front light.
changes.expected: Bands facing the softbox lift to about 170-195 at p95 while plessite stays below 70, giving the etched-metal sheen.

changes.problem: The lower third of the slice falls off too far, so the bottom bands go muddy.

evidence.measured: lum_median 76.6 against 130 in the middle third; y-profile of 1100,200-1400,1000: 111, 108, 104, 117, 129, 131, 88, 77.

changes.expected: Bottom of the slice holds about 90-110 median so the falloff top-to-bottom is under 30 levels rather than 54.

changes.problem: The left edge of the pocket shows no air rim: the sweep steps directly into the dark rind, so the slice looks cut out and pasted rather than sitting in an air pocket.

evidence.measured: edge step -42.6 over 5 px at offset 20, no bright band; the right rim (1625,580-1650,620) median 227, so the rim reads on one side only.

changes.expected: A 3-8 px light rim appears along the left and lower-left edge of the pocket, matching the right side.

changes.problem: Two tan parallelograms hang off the slice's left edge and read as stray stickers or a render artefact.

evidence.measured: median 198 (r211 g197 b172) against the sweep 237 (r244 g237 b223) next to it; a second patch at (275,800-300,815) median 214.

change.setting: trace and remove the source of the two tan patches (likely the left flag or the base's top refracted through the ball's lower-left)

changes.expected: The ground left of the slice is uniform sweep, within 6 levels of its surroundings.

changes.problem: The lower half of the ground is one flat value near white, so it reads blown and gives the frame no direction.

evidence.measured: lum_median 237.4, range 2.8; (0,900-400,1200) median 236.5, range 5.6; the frame's y-profile ends 233, 237.

changes.expected: The lower ground settles to about 215-228 with a visible gradient, still lighter than the slice, letting the green rim and the iron hold their edges.

changes.problem: The single vertical strip reflection lifts a 100 px band of the slice by 50+ levels and washes out the etch there, while being too soft to read as a polished acrylic highlight.
changes.expected: The streak stays visible as glass but the etch underneath keeps its band contrast; band median within about 15 levels of the surrounding slice.

out_of_scope.request: Make the pocket rim on the right read silver rather than mint.
out_of_scope.why: The rim (1635,590-1645,610) is rgb 216,228,210, delta-E 9.5 from a neutral silver #E4E6E6; its tint comes from the acrylic's measured absorption and the air void's TIR, both fixed. Light (c4) can make it brighter but not neutral.

out_of_scope.request: Pull the camera back or shorten the lens so a part of the ball's outer contour shows in a corner.
out_of_scope.why: The frame shows no ball at all, so 'sealed in acrylic' rests on one streak and one rim; this may conflict with the card's brief to be close on the slice, so it is the owner's framing call rather than a correction.
